owner: LocalFlow path ownership and bootstrap facade
problem: One root currently mixes administrator-owned configuration with service-instance runtime state, preventing explicit sharing and independent recovery.
scope: CLI bootstrap, application composition, configuration/auth repositories, task storage/logs, executor recovery, packaging, deployment and migration
baseline: create_app(root) and initialize_root(root) use the same directory for config, plugins, secrets, runtime, logs and exports
benchmarks: XDG Base Directory separates configuration, persistent state, cache and runtime files by ownership and lifetime
systemd.exec separates ConfigurationDirectory, StateDirectory, CacheDirectory, LogsDirectory and RuntimeDirectory
Prometheus and Grafana expose explicit storage/data paths independently from configuration inputs
advantages: Task recovery already uses durable SQLite and instance descriptors
disadvantages: A shared key/config tree cannot be paired with multiple independent histories
limitations: One operating-system port cannot be bound twice on the same host/address
Shared writable configuration has last-writer-wins external edits unless operators coordinate
defects: Frozen executable directory owns dynamic files
bottlenecks: Root is passed through composition rather than a typed path object
Systemd supervisor and log paths assume one root

hypotheses: A typed Roots value can split ownership without duplicating repository logic

hard_gates: No runtime/log/cache/port write below config root except an explicitly identical legacy mapping
Two instances share config bytes and keys but never database/log/port/descriptor bytes
Invalid state recovery cannot mutate config or secrets
Existing task working-directory resolution remains config-root relative
Release consumer runs a freshly downloaded archive
